title: Orbit setup assistant spec
description: One AI coding assistant configured by `orbit setup`, described as generic operations: detection paths, a managed instruction-file block, marker-owned JSON merges, templated files, string registrations, and skill directories. Each file's name field must match its file stem. Applied by crates/orbit-cli/src/commands/setup.

name.description: Assistant identifier accepted by `orbit setup <ASSISTANT>`. Must match the YAML file stem.

title.description: Display name shown in the setup wizard, e.g. Claude Code.

detect.description: Paths whose existence means the assistant is installed. `$VAR` reads an environment variable (skipped when unset), `~/` is the home directory.

instruction_file.description: Instruction file receiving the managed guidance block.

json_merges.description: Marker-owned merges into JSON arrays in the assistant's config, e.g. PreToolUse hooks.

template_files.description: Files written verbatim from an embedded config/setup/ template.

registrations.description: Strings appended to a JSON array in the assistant's config, e.g. a plugin list.

retired.description: Files and registrations an earlier release installed and this one no longer does. Install and uninstall remove them: a file only while its setup checksum shows it is unedited, and a registration by its value.

format.description: Layout of the MCP config: `claude` = mcpServers JSON, `codex` = [mcp_servers.<name>] TOML, `opencode` = mcp JSON.

mcp.description: Config file where an earlier release registered the `orbit` MCP server. Setup and uninstall remove that entry.

dir.description: Skills directory the assistant scans. The embedded skill is written to <dir>/<skill name>/.

link.description: Second skills directory that receives a symlink to the written skill, for assistants that do not scan `dir`.

requires_full.description: Install the full skill tree instead of the thin wrapper, for assistants that cannot run commands when they load a skill. Applies to every assistant sharing `dir`.

file.description: Settings file whose `permissions.allow` array receives the rules.

rules.description: Allow rules for the commands the installed skill runs. `{{orbit}}` expands to the launcher.

permissions.description: Allow rules that stop the assistant from asking before it runs the skill's commands.

skills.description: Where the embedded skill is installed on disk.

plugin.description: The plugin from packages/agent-plugins, written as a local marketplace, registered in the assistant's settings, and enabled. Installed by default; `--skip agent-plugins` opts out.

dir.description: Where the marketplace folder is written.

settings.description: Settings file that receives the extraKnownMarketplaces and enabledPlugins entries.

marketplace.description: Marketplace name setup writes to marketplace.json.

name.description: Plugin name, as the marketplace lists it.

min_version.description: Oldest assistant version that loads the plugin. Setup skips the plugin on an older or unreadable version.

version_command.description: Command whose output starts with the assistant's version, such as `claude --version`.

project.description: Path relative to the project root, used by --project/--dir.

global.description: Home-anchored user-config path, used by the default global scope. Either ~/path, or ${VAR:-~/default}/path where a non-empty absolute VAR replaces the default prefix.

marker.description: Substring identifying orbit-owned entries. Every entry must contain it in a nested string, otherwise re-running setup duplicates the entry instead of replacing it.

entries.description: Entries orbit owns at path. `{{orbit}}` in any nested string resolves to the launcher command.

ui.description: Installed with the agent-plugins component instead of hooks.

template.description: Template location under config/setup/, e.g. opencode_plugin.js.

ui.description: Removed with the agent-plugins component instead of hooks.
Installed with the agent-plugins component instead of hooks.

value.description: String appended to the array: project-relative in project scope, expanded absolute in global scope.

jsonPath.description: Object keys naming the target JSON array, outermost first.
